blockReview.observation: Experimental origin of the electric-field concept is preserved; no invented person or historical priority claim.
Electric force provides evidence about field distribution; the added limit on a single measurement avoids claiming it determines every field property.

Electrostatics is conditioned on a selected reference frame and time-independent stationary charge distribution. Time-dependent fields are not treated as universally electrostatic or detached from other fields/sources.
Small test-charge size, negligible source disturbance and electric-force rather than total-force measurement are explicit.

Fixed sources and the same observation point justify force proportionality to signed q. Magnitude proportionality is distinguished from the signed vector relation; no universal point-charge-only origin claim remains.
Equation8-11 is unchanged. Vector force divided by signed nonzero charge defines the electric-field vector; the following block supplies the nonzero condition.
Explicit nonzero test charge and exclusion of gravity/other forces make the definition operationally and algebraically sound.
Correctly introduces the electric-force relation at the charge's location without equating electric force with total force.
Equation8-12 preserves the signed vector relation F=qE.
Positive and negative probe-force directions follow from the sign of q. Field direction is independent of the probe sign, subject to the preceding negligible-perturbation condition.
SI electric-field unit N/C follows directly from equation8-11.

The scalar Coulomb form is confined to an ideal static homogeneous linear isotropic dielectric model, with boundary, finite-size and local effects neglected. A positive nonperturbing q0 is explicitly chosen.
Unchanged Coulomb force magnitude has absolute source/probe charges and inverse-square distance; its dimensions are force under the stated SI convention.
Positive-probe condition is repeated immediately before F/q0. For a negative probe, the text explicitly requires the charge magnitude as divisor when computing field magnitude.

Equation8-13 remains exactly printed, not silently repaired. With q0 positive, cancelling q0 from the preceding Coulomb magnitude gives the stated E. This is not endorsed as a magnitude formula for signed negative q0.
Point-source radial field points outward for a positive source and inward for a negative source; source q is distinguished from the earlier probe role. Figure113 reference is preserved.

Equation8-15 is the unchanged multiple-field vector sum, not a sum of scalar strengths.

The original overbroad noninteraction claim is corrected in prose: source charges may move or redistribute, and fields must then be recalculated. Fixed-point-charge calculation is limited to the earlier conditions; nonlinear media and the singular source point are excluded.

independentDerivations.result: At a fixed nonzero field, replacing probe q by -q reverses its electric force. Dividing the vector force by the signed charge leaves E unchanged. Dividing the force magnitude by a negative signed charge would not yield a nonnegative strength; the final text explicitly disallows that reading.

For the explicitly positive probe q0, |q0|=q0. Cancelling that factor in the unchanged Coulomb force magnitude yields |q|/(4*pi*epsilon0*epsilon*r^2). Thus the preserved F/q0 is sound under the stated positive-probe condition, without inventing an erratum.

Force divided by charge has unit N/C. The point-source SI expression has that dimension, and the final block excludes the source point where r=0. No new numerical value or calibration has been introduced.

With the same nonzero probe q and fixed sources, F1+F2=q(E1+E2); dividing by q gives the unchanged field sum at one observation point. A linear medium/fixed distribution permits this decomposition, but it does not prevent forces on source charges or charge redistribution.
